<!-- Do not edit: change the settings registry and regenerate this page. -->

This page is generated by `neon settings docs` from the server's settings registry.

Runtime settings apply without a restart. Each takes its value from the first of these
that has one:

1. its environment variable: `NEON_SETTINGS__` and the key in capitals, with `__` between
   levels, so `instance.name` is `NEON_SETTINGS__INSTANCE__NAME`
2. its key under `settings:` in the config file, `neon.yaml` or the file `NEON_CONFIG` names,
   one level per dot
3. the value saved in the database from the admin page
4. its default

A setting set by its environment variable or in the config file is pinned: the admin page
shows it but cannot change it.

A *set* holds some of its options: a list in the config file, such as `[user, agent]`, and
a comma-separated list in its environment variable, such as `user,agent`; empty is none.

Secret settings, and those that say where a secret goes, such as the mail server, are marked
*browser session only*: an admin changes them signed in at a browser, never with an API token.

| Key | Type | Default | Environment variable | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `auth.invite_email` | bool | `true` | `NEON_SETTINGS__AUTH__INVITE_EMAIL` | Admins can mail an invite to an address, naming themselves; only that address signs up with it, once, and counts as verified. Works while mail is set up. |
| `auth.invite_ttl` | duration | `7d` | `NEON_SETTINGS__AUTH__INVITE_TTL` | How long a new invite works, unless the admin making it sets its end. Applies to invites made from now. |
| `auth.min_password_length` | integer | `12` | `NEON_SETTINGS__AUTH__MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH` | The fewest characters a new password has. Passwords set before keep working. |
| `auth.password_reset` | bool | `true` | `NEON_SETTINGS__AUTH__PASSWORD_RESET` | Forgotten passwords can be reset with a link mailed to the account, working once for an hour. Setting the new password signs the account out everywhere. Works while mail is set up. |
| `auth.registration` | enum: open, invite, closed | `invite` | `NEON_SETTINGS__AUTH__REGISTRATION` | Who may create an account: anyone (open), people with an invite an admin made (invite), or nobody but admins, who add accounts themselves (closed). |
| `auth.request_denied_mail` | bool | `true` | `NEON_SETTINGS__AUTH__REQUEST_DENIED_MAIL` | Mail people whose request to join an admin denied, saying they may ask again in 30 days. Off, a denied request just closes. |
| `auth.requests` | bool | `false` | `NEON_SETTINGS__AUTH__REQUESTS` | While registration is by invite, people without one can ask for it with a note. They confirm their address by a mailed link first; admins then approve, which mails them an invite, or deny. Needs mail set up first: see mail.enabled. |
| `auth.session_absolute_ttl` | duration | `30d` | `NEON_SETTINGS__AUTH__SESSION_ABSOLUTE_TTL` | A browser session signs out this long after it started, however active it is. Applies to sessions started from now. |
| `auth.session_idle_ttl` | duration | `7d` | `NEON_SETTINGS__AUTH__SESSION_IDLE_TTL` | A browser session unused this long signs out. Applies to sessions in use from now. |
| `auth.verify_email` | bool | `false` | `NEON_SETTINGS__AUTH__VERIFY_EMAIL` | People who sign up themselves get a link by mail and can sign in once they open it; an account still unverified after 7 days is removed. Those who sign up with an invite mailed to them, and accounts admins make, count as verified. Needs mail set up first: see mail.enabled. |
| `instance.name` | string | `Neon Teamspace` | `NEON_SETTINGS__INSTANCE__NAME` | The instance's name, shown in the interface and in mail. |
| `mail.enabled` | bool | `false` | `NEON_SETTINGS__MAIL__ENABLED` | Sends mail through the SMTP server mail.host names. Mail is set up once this is on and mail.host and mail.from are set. Mail also needs server.public_url, which its links point to, and secrets.keys, which seals it while it waits in the queue. |
| `mail.from` | string | empty | `NEON_SETTINGS__MAIL__FROM` | The address mail comes from, such as neon@example.com. The SMTP server must let the account send as it, and its domain needs SPF, DKIM and DMARC records for mail to arrive. |
| `mail.from_name` | string | empty | `NEON_SETTINGS__MAIL__FROM_NAME` | The name shown beside the From address. Empty uses instance.name. |
| `mail.host` | string | empty | `NEON_SETTINGS__MAIL__HOST` | The SMTP server mail goes through, such as smtp.example.com: a host name or an IP address, without a scheme or port. *Browser session only.* |
| `mail.notifications` | bool | `true` | `NEON_SETTINGS__MAIL__NOTIFICATIONS` | Mails people about activity that concerns them, while mail is set up: for now, admins hear of each confirmed request to join. Off, they see requests on the admin page only. |
| `mail.password` | secret | empty | `NEON_SETTINGS__MAIL__PASSWORD` | The password of that account. Saved here, it is kept encrypted, which needs secrets.keys. *Browser session only.* |
| `mail.port` | integer | `587` | `NEON_SETTINGS__MAIL__PORT` | The SMTP server's port: 587 for starttls, 465 for tls, 25 or a relay's own for none. *Browser session only.* |
| `mail.tls` | enum: starttls, tls, none | `starttls` | `NEON_SETTINGS__MAIL__TLS` | How the connection is secured. starttls upgrades it with STARTTLS and refuses a server that does not offer it; tls speaks TLS from the start; none stays plain, for a relay on this host or a network you trust. TLS is 1.2 or later, and the server's certificate is always checked. A password is never sent over a plain connection, except to this host. *Browser session only.* |
| `mail.username` | string | empty | `NEON_SETTINGS__MAIL__USERNAME` | The account to sign in to the SMTP server with. Empty for a server that takes mail without signing in. *Browser session only.* |
| `pages.trash_retention` | duration | `30d` | `NEON_SETTINGS__PAGES__TRASH_RETENTION` | How long a page stays in the trash, with the pages trashed along with it, before the hourly cleanup deletes it for good. Until then, those who could edit it restore it. Applies to the whole trash at the next cleanup. |
| `workspaces.creation` | enum: anyone, admins | `anyone` | `NEON_SETTINGS__WORKSPACES__CREATION` | Who may create a workspace: every account (anyone), or instance admins only (admins). Workspaces made before a change stay. |
| `workspaces.limits.agents` | integer | `0` | `NEON_SETTINGS__WORKSPACES__LIMITS__AGENTS` | The most agents a workspace has, unless an instance admin sets its own limit; 0 is no limit. Kept for agents, which are not built yet. |
| `workspaces.limits.members` | integer | `0` | `NEON_SETTINGS__WORKSPACES__LIMITS__MEMBERS` | The most people a workspace holds, guests included, unless an instance admin sets its own limit; 0 is no limit. A workspace at its limit refuses invitations, accepting them and joining by link; nobody in it is removed. |
| `workspaces.limits.storage_bytes` | integer | `0` | `NEON_SETTINGS__WORKSPACES__LIMITS__STORAGE_BYTES` | The most bytes a workspace's attachments take, unless an instance admin sets its own limit; 0 is no limit. Kept for attachments, which are not built yet. |
